svg.text: Packed instructions: eight lanes in one register
Custom-0 group "xcompute" (Riscv64 parameter XCOMPUTE). A 64-bit register holds 8 bytes or 4 16-bit numbers; one instruction works on all of them at once.
1. paddus.b rd, rs1, rs2: 8 saturating byte adds (brighten, additive blending)
No carry crosses a lane boundary: eight 9-bit adders
side by side, each shallower than one 64-bit add.
Pink: the sum passed 255, so the lane stops at ff
(plain adds would wrap a bright pixel to black).
Runs in MEMORY alone, like every custom instruction.
2. pdot.b rd, rs1, rs2: a dot product of 8 signed bytes, split between EXECUTE and MEMORY
Each product: 9 partial-product rows in a carry-save
tree (4 levels), then one 16-bit prefix add.
(full adders: no carry runs along the word)
the dot product, written to rd and
A whole 8-lane multiply-and-sum is too deep for one clock next to
everything else; split like this, each half fits (docs/XCOMPUTE.md).
